Hi,

there certainly seems to some memory issues, as the error message
says. I guess this is due to the layout of the exon arrays, i.e.
there are some units with a very-large number of probes (although I
haven't verified this). Try setting the 'ram' argument of fit() to a
smaller than number than the default 1, e.g.

fit(plm, ram=0.3, verbose=verbose).

That should do. Already fitted units should not be refitted.

Cheers

Henrik

parts:
Hi,

yes try to restart. It never hurts to restart - also,
aroma.affymetrix remembers what's already processed and skips that.
Also try a smaller 'ram' value if it happens again.

Again, when you see "Failed to read the CDF file." that message comes
from affxparser and is because its internal Affymetrix Fusion SDK
library fails to initiate the CDF for reading, which in turn (from our
recent experience) is likely to happen when you run out of memory.

Operation system crash course: R runs as a *process* in Windows/Unix.
All memory allocation by R, its packages and the packages internal
library is done in the process shared memory. If some of the code
fails to clean up the memory, the only way to get that memory back is
to terminate the process, that is, to terminate R and start a new R
session. R itself and packages written in plain R, such as
aroma.affymetrix et al, utilizes the built in R garbage collector to
clean out the memory and there should be no issues with that one. My
*guess* is that Fusion SDK does not deallocate the memory allocated
when it runs out of memory; meaning there are allocated memory blocks
that won't be freed until you restart R.

/H
